author: alfred
text: I am retired and this investment tops up my pension every month. I cannot afford to see the capital go down.

author: alfred
text: I want to try very volatile stocks to make money quickly, but I need this money to pay my tuition fees in September.

author: alfred
text: This is my emergency fund. I want to be able to get it back at any time, without any loss, in case something unexpected happens.

author: alfred
text: I am preparing a project in four or five years. A 5% drop does not bother me, but beyond 10% I would start to worry.

author: alfred
text: I want a bit more than a savings account over the next few years, mostly bonds with a small share of shares. Large swings would worry me.

author: alfred
text: I am investing for my children's education in ten years. I want growth, but I would keep about half in more stable assets.

author: alfred
text: Horizon of six to eight years. I have already lived through a 15% fall without selling anything, but a 40% drop would make me reduce my positions.

author: alfred
text: I am 25 and I invest part of my salary every month for my retirement. Crashes are chances to buy cheaper.

author: alfred
text: I will not need this inheritance for at least twenty years. I aim for maximum return and I accept that the portfolio may lose half of its value along the way.

author: alfred
text: My income as an entrepreneur more than covers my needs. This money can stay invested in stocks for the long term, even in a very turbulent market.
